meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'alcohol' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And what if he refuses alcohol?

examples.text: Вы хотите добавить алкоголь в еду?
examples.trans: Do you want to add alcohol to food?

meanings.note: Habitually or in general. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

instrumental of вечер used as an adverb

examples.trans: I'm at home in the evening.

meanings.en: to throw out, to toss out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брасывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to throw out', paired with 'выбросить'.

examples.trans: Throwing a person out the window is not normal!

examples.text: Иван Васильевич, выбрасывать человека в окно нормально?
examples.trans: Ivan Vasilyevich, is throwing a person out the window normal?

examples.text: А что вы предлагаете? Всех чиновников в окно выбрасывать?
examples.trans: And what do you propose? Throwing all officials out the window?

выпить.gloss: to drink (up); to have a drink

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink of
meanings.note: + accusative or partitive genitive. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drink (up); to have a drink', paired with 'пить'.

Used without an object. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drink (up); to have a drink', paired with 'пить'.

examples.trans: May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

examples.text: Милый, можно я выпью капельку пива?
examples.trans: Darling, may I drink a tiny drop of beer?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hands', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Денис, откуда у тебя в руках живой голубь?
examples.trans: Denis, where did you get a live pigeon in your hands?

examples.text: Так, друзья, где мой голубь по-дижонски?
examples.trans: All right, folks, where is my Dijon squab?

examples.text: Откуда под крышкой взялся этот живой голубь?
examples.trans: Where did that live pigeon under the cover come from?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'restaurant', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Разве в нашем ресторане гости едят голубей?
examples.trans: Do guests really eat pigeons in our restaurant?

examples.text: Нет, только не трогай этих дорогих голубей!
examples.trans: No, just do not touch those expensive pigeons!

examples.text: Пожалуйста, отдай мне хотя бы одного голубя!
examples.trans: Please give me back at least one pigeon!

meanings.note: Untamed. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wild, terrible').
Colloquial intensifier. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wild, terrible').

examples.trans: Wild animals live in the forest.

examples.text: Я хочу извиниться за вчерашнее. Просто отошёл наркоз, и были дикие боли.
examples.trans: I want to apologise for yesterday. The anaesthesia just wore off, and I had wild pain.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рого'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Французские десерты всегда стоят очень дорого.
examples.trans: French desserts always cost very much.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

издеваться.gloss: to mock, to kid, to mess with

meanings.en: to mock, to tease; colloquially 'are you kidding me?'
meanings.note: Ты что, издеваешься? = Are you kidding me?
Common feminine noun meaning 'sweet, piece of candy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here, I bought some sweets for the kids.

examples.text: Вот детям конфет купил. А семья и без меня хорошо время проводит!
examples.trans: Here, I bought sweets for the kids. And the family is having a good time without me!

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('best; better').

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are torturing yourselves / struggling'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и мучиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and are torturing yourselves on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют мучиться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to are torturing yourselves.

related.gloss: not to are torturing yourselves (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: Parenthetical adverb. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').
Colloquial. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'близости').

examples.trans: There is another maternity hospital nearby.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно поблизости и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite nearby and calmly.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.en: to make up, to make peace
meanings.note: Помириться с кем + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мириться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to make up, to reconcile', paired with 'мириться'.

examples.text: Когда-нибудь ты захочешь помириться со своим папой.
examples.trans: Someday you will want to make up with your dad.

examples.text: Я сто раз хотела с ним помириться!
examples.trans: I wanted to make up with him a hundred times!

examples.text: Хорошо, я согласна помириться с тобой.
examples.trans: Good, I agree to make peace with you.

meanings.en: to try, to have a go
meanings.note: + infinitive. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.text: Как я могу это забыть? Ну, давай попробуем.
examples.trans: How can I forget that? Well, let's try.

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: 'один раз' = once, 'два раза' = twice

Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слабиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to relax', paired with 'расслабляться'.

examples.text: Ваня, расслабься. В этот раз без обмана.
examples.trans: Vanya, relax. This time there's no trick.

meanings.note: Not occurring often. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('rare, scarce, unusual').

examples.text: У меня есть много редких материалов.
Макс, почему редкие трюфели оказались на помойке?
examples.trans: Max, why did rare truffles end up in the dumpster?

examples.text: Но вы обязаны распробовать этот редкий шедевр!
examples.trans: But you must taste this rare masterpiece!

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оюзник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'ally' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A man's best ally is alcohol.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть союзник.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always ally.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Бросить трубку = to hang up. Common feminine noun meaning '(phone) receiver; tube' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning '(phone) receiver; tube' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'fillet', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('tenderloin') (choice tender meat cut) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Главное, не пережарь это нежное филе.
examples.trans: The main thing is do not overcook this tender fillet.

examples.text: Сначала удалить хребет и охладить филе?
examples.trans: First remove the backbone and chill the fillet?

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Irregular plural цветы (flowers). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'flower' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Fresh flowers stood in the window.
Congratulations to you! Konstantin, give her the flowers.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
